test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2023: Official Paper (Held On: 17 Aug, 2023 Shift 4)
subject: general
question: The founders of the Vijayanagara Empire were the feudatories of which of the following dynasties?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kakatiya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The founders of the Vijayanagara Empire** were the **feudatories Kakatiya dynasty**.
 
• Before establishing the Vijayanagara Empire in **1336, Harihara and Bukka**, who were initially feudatories of the Kakatiyas of Warangal, served in administrative roles for both the Kakatiya and Kampili kingdoms.
 
• Following the Muslim conquest of Kakatiya in 1323, they sought refuge in Kampili, where they eventually rose to become ministers.
 
• The Vijayanagara Empire, founded by Harihara and Bukka, emerged after their time in Kampili.
 
• Over its history, the empire saw the rule of significant dynasties including the** Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Hoysala Empire**, a significant Kannadiga power in the Indian subcontinent, held sway over much of present-day Karnataka from the 10th to the 14th centuries. Initially headquartered in Belur, the capital later shifted to Halebidu.
 
• **The Pandyan dynasty,** also known as the Pandyas of Madurai, stood as an ancient Tamil dynasty in South India, counted among the prominent kingdoms of Tamilakam alongside the Pallavas, the Cholas, and the Cheras.
 
• Originating from southern India, the **Chola dynasty** governed the expansive Chola Empire, a prominent maritime power. The earliest verifiable mentions of the Chola date back to inscriptions dating to the 3rd century BCE during the Maurya empire under Ashoka's reign.
